prerequisite_contract.accepted: v10-c08 dividend-adjusted vanilla formula, funded PDE and parity; v10-c07 restricted scalar localized Ito for continuous adapted coefficients, positive paths and deterministic time/parameter transformations.
prerequisite_contract.coordination: Confirmed tau=T-t, calendar Theta=-C_tau and fixed-input Greeks with c10/c11 authors. C10 may use finite positive-vega interval conditioning; c11 may use fixed-model-vol funded mismatch under the stated diffusion scope. No general random volatility-surface dynamics, Girsanov theorem, tree convergence or jump replication is smuggled into c09.

proof_audit: Derived delta/gamma/vega/calendar theta by A phi(d1)=H phi(d2); put adjustments follow differentiated parity. Units, volatility point scaling, position signs and nonuniversal theta sign are explicit. Same S/sigma/tau vega-gamma identity proves a rank restriction, not universal portfolio interchangeability.

Multivariate Taylor is applied to the line segment with continuous third derivatives in a compact interior region. Abbreviated delta/gamma/vega/theta approximation omits mixed Hessian terms. Independent analytic spot-only C_SSS supremum bound is derived from monotone d1 and bounded normal density; it does not purport to cover mixed shocks.

Calibrated total first/second derivatives follow the chain rule under a declared twice differentiable spot response. Cross-sectional strike skew alone does not identify spot dynamics or prove a replication rule.

Positive vega proves strict monotonicity in sigma; normal-argument endpoint limits and the intermediate-value theorem prove the exact open quote range and uniqueness. Zero spot, strike or maturity fail strict identification. Mean-value inverse bound requires a positive lower vega throughout the solution interval. Floating-point/cap/near-boundary statuses do not assert interval certification.

Strike monotonicity, discounted Lipschitz bounds and weighted convexity are payoff comparisons under matched executable rights. Unequal-strike weights and full piecewise butterfly payoff verified; finite passing screens are not a full dynamic arbitrage-free surface theorem.

Every discrete hedge reset preserves incoming stock plus bank less fees. Dividend shares grow continuously under the specified frictionless reinvestment rule. Cash is not replaced by the model mark. Fees are debited at payment date and accrue thereafter. Terminal liquidation and written payoff have correct signs even on the losing path.

For actual positive continuous diffusion with continuous adapted coefficients and fixed pricing sigma, subtracting funded gains and actual-path Ito cancels physical drift/diffusion terms and yields dE=rE dt+Gamma*S^2*(sigma_model^2-a^2)dt/2. Discounting is explicit. Localized bounded integrands and integrable pathwise 1/sqrt(T-t) cash-gamma majorant justify terminal extension; expectations need additional integrability. Negative q can be covered by exp(abs(q)*T). No unproved process-existence or arbitrary-predictable-coefficient theorem is assumed.

The weighted two-slice variance example is algebra with supplied weights, not two claimed diffusion realizations. Continuous mismatch is not an exact discrete realized-variance identity; the discrete expansion retains mixed/time/spatial remainder effects and excludes fees, changed marks and jumps.

Central-difference delta/gamma bounds include both smooth truncation and bounded evaluation error. The optimal delta perturbation is derived analytically, with an explicit smooth-domain and actual-price-error condition. Numerical grid refinement is a diagnostic rather than proof of these smoothness assumptions.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic examples and an idealized continuous-yield European contract; no empirical quote/hedge validation or executable-market claim.
Double precision can underflow in extreme tails; numerical bisection brackets and Simpson refinement are not interval arithmetic or a global error certificate.
The lab rejects boundary base Greek inputs and distinguishes model boundary prices internally. General stochastic-volatility, jumps and altered payout/funding require additional models.
